races.name: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Claiming Hurdle

runners_data.name: Jackson Lamb
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for John McConnell, has form on good ground over this sort of trip but wears a hood and carries 168lbs; the 18-day turnaround is fine but a recent form string of 0-P752 is not encouraging, and sharing the lead with Rocky's Howya may simply drain the engine before the finish.|

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's five-year-old arrives on an 11-day turnaround having won recently, rates highly on OR 117, and the sim-going record (13/15) shows it handles these conditions well; a hold-up horse by nature but the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 2/23 is modest, so the horse needs to do the talking.|

runners_data.name: Rich Belief
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's nine-year-old has placed at this course-and-distance configuration before and its two wins have come on good ground; genuine hold-up horse who needs the race to be run fast enough to bring the field back to it, and at 158lbs over 2m4½f on 20 days' rest that is a reasonable ask.|

runners_data.name: Allo Al Khawaneej
runners_data.note: C Byrnes' six-year-old is a natural rear-division horse by profile but the congested field means it is unlikely to get its preferred unpressured position; its sim-going record (11/14) suggests conditions are workable, though 30 days since last run and a form line of 387-40 give little current confidence.|

runners_data.name: Bryson
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for W R Crawford's yard whose best recent effort (2nd) came at this trip on good ground, but the form string of 6-U267 since then is uninspiring; pushed into a midfield role it would not naturally occupy, and the 5lb claimer (James Smith) cannot compensate for a structural disadvantage.|

runners_data.name: Rocky's Howya
runners_data.note: Declan Queally's ten-year-old is a confirmed front-runner who has won at 2m4f on good ground and comes in on 24 days' rest wearing a visor; the key question is whether it can see off Jackson Lamb early enough to control tempo, and at OR 116 and 152lbs it retains competitive claims if it does.|

runners_data.name: Eastern Wind
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride on T G McCourt's seven-year-old, whose two placed efforts came on shorter trips and better ground; a natural prominent-type horse operating away from its best, and the form line of 4090-9 underlines that it has not threatened recently — the style mismatch compounds that.|

runners_data.name: Movie King
runners_data.note: V C Ward's nine-year-old has shown only modest form (best effort a third) and the trainer has no recorded winners in the 14-day window; not a natural midfield settler and at OR 82 would need a dramatic collapse in the field to get competitive, even with a 7lb claimer.|

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane's nine-year-old is a hold-up horse by habit with an exceptional sim-going record (14/15) and three wins in the last five completions at this type of trip; Eoghan Finegan rides and the 13-day return looks sharp, making this one of the more interesting profiles if the pace genuinely rolls.|

runners_data.name: Howdoyalikeherhome
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's seven-year-old goes in trip-and-ground-friendly conditions (14/15 sim-going), wears a hood, and has placed at this distance before; Joshua Halford takes a 7lb claim which helps the weight, and the Elliott yard (1/31 in the 14-day window) is relatively cold but this horse has recent placed form.|

runners_data.name: Long Gone
runners_data.note: Noel Kelly's eight-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse with an outstanding sim-going record (15/15) and three wins at this level, but the redistribution means it will be closer to the pace than suits its style; Conor Stone-Walsh rides and the 16-day return is fine, though the form of 1P-6P0 most recently raises freshness questions.|

runners_data.name: Malbas
runners_data.note: Edward Buckley's ten-year-old has a perfect sim-going record (15/15) but the form line of 98-090 and the flagged tendency to fade in the finish are both significant negatives; at OR 97 and carrying 146lbs, displaced from its natural position, it holds limited appeal even if conditions theoretically suit.|

runners_data.name: Oh So Charming
runners_data.note: Declan Queally's six-year-old won recently at 18f on good ground and the sim-going record (14/15) is solid; a horse whose natural position is further back than the map can accommodate, but the recent win and lower weight (146lbs) make it one of the more credible redistributed runners if the early pace truly sets up a late swoop.|

runners_data.name: Beacon Bypass
runners_data.note: Paul Mulligan's four-year-old is the youngest in the field and returns just seven days after its last run; the fading-in-finish flag is a serious concern over 2m4½f, the form line shows no top-three finish in five starts, and being the lightest in the race (142lbs) cannot offset a profile that struggles to see out the trip.

races.paceDynamic: Jackson Lamb and Rocky's Howya are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over this 2m4½f trip on Good to Yielding ground, creating an honest, pressured gallop that is unlikely to relent across the long Bellewstown straight. With two genuine pace-setters duelling, the race will be run at a true clip from flag to finish, burning off any horse that tries to track them too close without the engine to sustain it. This contested pace scenario classically sets up the race for prominent-to-midfield types who can settle just off the pressure and hit the rising ground with a full tank — horses like Tassarolo, Mephisto, and Howdoyalikeherhome carry the profile that benefits most from a genuinely run race at this trip. This field also contains substantially more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Long Gone, Allo Al Khawaneej, Eastern Wind, Movie King, Malbas, Oh So Charming, and Beacon Bypass are all genuine hold-up or prominent horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the pace picture pushes them off their natural position, with Jackson Lamb and Rocky's Howya the only runners realistically assured of their preferred ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Midfield Finishers
scenarios.trigger: If Jackson Lamb and Rocky's Howya push each other through a genuine gallop and leave the race wide open for a well-conserved run from behind the pace.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners take the sting out of each other over the extended trip on yielding ground, handing the race to runners who tracked at an economical distance and finish strongest up the hill; Tassarolo and Mephisto carry class, course-going fitness, and the right profile to capitalise on a truly run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Howya repels Jackson Lamb early, asserts control, and finds a rhythm that allows it to dictate without burning excessive fuel.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Howya has won at this trip on good ground and has shown the ability to control a race from the front when allowed to bowl along at its own pace; if Jackson Lamb cannot match its stride and drops away, the veteran front-runner could steal enough daylight to hold on.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns fiercely enough to bring true stamina to the fore and several midfield runners also fade, leaving room for the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: Howdoyalikeherhome and Rich Belief have the form figures and going evidence to suggest they stay this trip well and could pick up late if the race is truly run ragged; note that several nominal hold-up runners are displaced from their natural position and may not be as effective as true closers in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Compact Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Jackson Lamb and Rocky's Howya settle into a mutualistic rhythm rather than a genuine duel, producing a falsely run race that compresses the field.
scenarios.body: A slower early tempo would allow the larger midfield pack to stay in contention throughout and produce a bunched finish where class off the ratings edge out; Tassarolo's higher OR and recent winning form give it the edge in a messy scramble, though redistributed hold-up types racing out of role would remain disadvantaged.

watchPoints.text: Rocky's Howya and Jackson Lamb — watch the first two flights closely; if Jackson Lamb applies sustained pressure and Rocky's Howya cannot shake free within the first mile, both front-runners could come back to the field exhausted before the final turn.|

Tassarolo — watch its position entering the back straight; if Daniel King gets it tucked in four or five lengths off the pace with cover, it is ideally placed to exploit the contested tempo and its recent fitness edge over an older, heavier field is significant.|

Mephisto — watch for Eoghan Finegan positioning it to travel smoothly in rear; if the pace is as fierce as predicted the horse's stamina and sim-going record make it dangerous late, but it needs the race to be truly run and cannot do it from an unprepared position.|

Long Gone — despite its excellent ground record (15/15) and three wins at this level, watch whether Conor Stone-Walsh can get it settled away from trouble early; if the redistribution forces it into a position three or four places closer than ideal, it may use energy it needs for the finish.|

Beacon Bypass — a four-year-old running seven days after its last start with a noted tendency to fade; watch for it being eased out of contention from the third-last as an indicator that the pace has been genuinely fierce and the race is about to be decided among the better-class hold-up types.|

races.name: Bet With Tote On Racing & Sports Maiden Hurdle
Money Back Daily Specials With Tote.ie Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cornaroya Rocco
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for John Joseph Hanlon who goes well on this ground (8/8 similar going), but 2m4½f in a big field from the rear demands a perfect passage; 16 days since last run is fine, but his best RPR finishes have come in smaller fields where gaps appear more readily.

runners_data.name: Goin'
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with solid similar-going form (14/15) and placed last time at Listowel, but a string of mid-pack finishes suggests he finds one too good rather than winning; 26 days fresh, and the headgear (ht) is unchanged — this trip and ground are fine but the style mismatch in a large field is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Gforcejenny
runners_data.note: Cromwell has a strong 7/28 trainer strike rate over the last 14 days, and this four-year-old has placed at 2m on soft; returns after 78 days off which is the biggest flag — hold-up style means she needs cover early and may need the run after such a layoff.

runners_data.name: Hatfield Hammer
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won over this trip and handles Good ground (1W7P similar going); Paul Nolan send him here freshened up after 34 days, Eoin Staples claims 5lb which is valuable in a handicap — naturally suited to sitting just behind the leader and this is his ideal race shape.

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton (7lb claimer) takes over for the veteran's ninth season; hold-up style has produced consistent placed form on Good ground (14/15) but no wins and a tendency to finish fourth or sixth rather than challenging; 10 days between runs is tight.

runners_data.name: Steps In The Sand
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with the most wins of any runner from similar going (3W5P over 15 runs) and stays 2m4f well — the combination of proven course fitness, a genuine tactical style, and a straightforward weight of 161lbs makes him one of the key threats to Dunany Point.

runners_data.name: Memories Maker
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's five-year-old is a true hold-up horse pushed into a midfield map slot by the sheer volume of rear-runners; recent form is poor (P last time) and the style fit score of 0.90 reflects genuine concern that he cannot replicate his second-placed effort if he cannot get to the back of the field naturally.

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: McCann's other runner, also a hold-up type with a ⚠ fade flag; five of five similar-going runs have produced mid-table finishes and he has never threatened to win — even if he gets his position, the fade flag is a significant negative in the final half-mile.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Serenade
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by nature whose second place over 2m4f in similar going stands out in an otherwise modest record; the redistribution to midfield means Thomas Coyle's six-year-old is likely jostling for position rather than dropping out where he travels best, and STYLE_FIT 0.91 tempers expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: Dunany Point
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner and therefore master of his own destiny; his last three runs include a third and a seventh, and his best recent effort (3rd at Galway) came when he was allowed to bowl along — Kieren Buckley simply needs to control the gallop and avoid being swallowed up at the last two hurdles.

runners_data.name: Pillartou
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up horse with a ⚠ fade flag who has never placed in three hurdle starts — all on Good ground; Jack Gilligan (5lb) claims but the combination of a STYLE_FIT penalty, a fading tendency, and a completely clean form record makes this a very difficult profile to back in this scenario.

runners_data.name: Avec Espoir
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old prominent racer for V T O'Brien with three career wins over similar going, though the last win came years ago; runs prominently which is the right approach in this race shape, but an OR of 80 and a string of pulls-up and last-place finishes signal the veteran is past his best.

runners_data.name: Mr Macphisto
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins over similar going (2W4P) and stays this trip; 54 days between runs is the main query, and at ten years old he needs things to go his way — positioned prominently he at least gets a sight of the pace and can take advantage if the lead group weakens.

runners_data.name: Ardgillan
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a ⚠ fade flag and poor recent form (7900-0); redistributed to midfield due to the crowded rear, and with a STYLE_FIT penalty, 18 days between runs on a trip he has only handled moderately, the overall picture is unpromising.

runners_data.name: Grace's Legacy
runners_data.note: Four-year-old filly whose best effort of fifth came over 2m on Soft; the 106-day break is the stand-out flag — she carries a ⚠ fade and is redistributed to midfield away from her natural role, making it hard to construct a positive case on return from such a long absence.

runners_data.name: Glenriver
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old whose highest STYLE_FIT redistribution score (0.93) in this field reflects that he is one of the most natural rear-runners of all, making midfield occupation particularly unnatural; ⚠ fade flag and a winless hurdles career in recent form suggest he is here to complete.

runners_data.name: Midleton Rare
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 99 and three wins over similar going (3W3P), including a win at 2m4f — the form figure of 1 is buried in his history but is there; hold-up style and no jockey listed is a notable negative, and a run of poor recent form (10th, 9th, pulled up) clouds what the rating suggests.

runners_data.name: Balinaboola Steel
runners_data.note: Fourteen-year-old returning after a remarkable 738 days off — by far the longest absence in the field; the STYLE_FIT redistribution score of 0.93 underlines how deeply he wants to race at the rear, and even with placed form in his past, this is an enormous ask at his age after such a break.

runners_data.name: Magic Hands Noel
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with all four hurdle starts producing double-figure finishes, three of them on Heavy or Soft ground he clearly did not handle; the ⚠ fade flag, STYLE_FIT redistribution penalty, 223-day layoff, and completely winless profile combine to make this the most challenging profile in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Dunany Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 19-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pressure from another confirmed leader — this means he can dictate his own rhythm from the front at a pace that suits himself over 2m4½f on Good to Yielding ground. The prominent types Hatfield Hammer, Steps In The Sand, Avec Espoir, and Mr Macphisto will push forward to claim positions just off the pace, creating a race run at a genuine but not brutally fast gallop — comfortable enough for Dunany Point to control, yet sufficient to stretch any hold-up horses who must make up significant ground late. With the majority of this field being true hold-up horses, the field is heavily rear-loaded, and the combination of a sustainable front-running pace and a big field means closers will face a wall of horses and a long run home that will test their ability to find a clear passage. This race shape unambiguously favours horses racing prominently or from just off the pace, as the controlled gallop will preserve energy for the finish and the prominent-to-midfield runners will have the best view of the race from three out. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the rear of the map can accommodate — Memories Maker, Whiskey Serenade, Pillartou, Ardgillan, Grace's Legacy, Glenriver, and Balinaboola Steel are all genuine hold-up types unable to fulfil their natural role, and of these Memories Maker and Whiskey Serenade are most likely to force their way into a tracking position, though that itself is no guarantee.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dunany Point Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point bowls along uncontested and the prominent horses are content to track without applying pressure.
scenarios.body: Dunany Point sets a sustainable pace on ground he handles, reaches the final hurdle full of running, and kicks on — the honest but not brutal pace means he is not emptied out before the straight; prominent trackers Hatfield Hammer and Steps In The Sand are ideally placed to chase but lack the finishing kick to catch a horse who has had everything his own way.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point weakens from two out and the prominent trackers Hatfield Hammer and Steps In The Sand sweep past in the straight.
scenarios.body: The pace is honest enough to expose Dunany Point's limitations in the closing stages, and the horses who have travelled smoothly just off the pace inherit the advantage at exactly the right moment; Steps In The Sand's course form and Hatfield Hammer's experience at this trip make them natural beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the lead group tie each other up, allowing a well-positioned midfield horse to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Midleton Rare, who has the highest OR in the field and placed form at this trip, is the most credible midfield beneficiary if the prominent group overcook it; Cornaroya Rocco and Goin', genuine hold-up types who handle this going well, could also arrive late if a gap materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Closers Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop quickens sharply on the final circuit and the prominent group come back to the field, opening the race for deep hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: This depends on horses racing out of their natural position — Memories Maker and Whiskey Serenade are redistributed from hold-up to midfield and would need the race to fall perfectly for them; the ⚠ fade flags on most deep closers in this field further reduce the chance of a late swooper landing this.

watchPoints.text: Dunany Point carries the entire pace map on his own — if Kieren Buckley is bumped or hampered at the start or early on, the race loses its shape entirely and the prominent horses behind him may overreach in a rush to the front.

Steps In The Sand and Hatfield Hammer are both genuine prominent types who will compete for the same position just off Dunany Point — watch whether one settles behind the other or whether they push each other wide and fast in the early stages, which would change the energy equation for both.

With nine runners carrying a REDISTRIBUTED flag, early positioning will be chaotic — horses including Memories Maker and Whiskey Serenade will be seeking to drop out but may be trapped in traffic, and any shuffling on the first circuit over hurdles in a 19-runner field carries elevated fall risk.

Midleton Rare has the highest official rating and a winning run over this distance in his form, but runs without a listed jockey confirmed — any last-minute rider change or inexperienced conditional should be treated as a material downgrade to his chance.

Grace's Legacy and Balinaboola Steel both return from very long absences (106 and 738 days respectively) — even if either shows ability on the day, their fitness levels relative to runners in better form rhythm are an obvious watch point for punters constructing exotics.

races.name: Bective Stud, Hotel & Tea Rooms Mullacurry Cup Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Red Glory
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's stable in solid form at T14 9/36; has won at this distance over similar ground and brings 3W8P sim-going record but is naturally a prominent racer whose STYLE_FIT of 0.92 flags it as racing slightly out of role at the head of affairs — monitor whether it can sustain front-running over 2m4½f.|

runners_data.name: Chanceawetmorning
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott second string here with James Smith (5) up; form string shows 1-3-1-9-3 and has placed at 2m4f on soft, making distance and going a clear fit, and prominent style slots naturally into the likely race shape.|

runners_data.name: Dreal Deal
runners_data.note: 11-year-old veteran for P J Rothwell in fine T14 form (3/10); placed over 2m4f on good going and is a genuine hold-up horse whose patient style could suit if the pace is truly searching — apprentice Clarke (7) needs to judge the race well from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Liam Swagger
runners_data.note: Only 5-year-old in the field with a hg:tp tongue-tie and impressive 2W8P sim-going record; prominent style fits the projected shape naturally, though a drop from 16f to this sharp 2m4½f trip invites a stamina question on only second run beyond 14f.|

runners_data.name: Final Orders
runners_data.note: Returning after 137 days off for Gavin Cromwell, who has hit 7/28 in the last 14 days; proven in stamina tests over 2m6f-2m4f on soft, and hold-up style gives Keith Donoghue options, though the layoff is the key concern at an age (10) where fitness matters.|

runners_data.name: Avalo
runners_data.note: Mark Walsh takes the ride for Peter Fahey, whose yard is quiet at T14 0/9; won over 16f on good ground and has placed twice over 2m4f, but a 12th and 17th on soft/heavy questions suitability if the ground rides slower than advertised — hold-up style needs the pace to be genuine.|

runners_data.name: Theflyingbee
runners_data.note: Consistent front-end performer with five recent top-three finishes and a sim-going record of 11/15; sits at the lower end of the weights (157lbs, OR 117) which is an asset, and prominent style is a natural fit for the projected race shape, though winning form is harder to find (1W6P).|

runners_data.name: Arctic Flame
runners_data.note: Unbeaten at 2m4f on good going (1/20f/GOO) and has placed twice in similar conditions — genuinely interesting form angle. However, Arctic Flame is a true hold-up horse carried into midfield on the map due to the volume of closers in this field; Torrens must navigate the race carefully from a position that is not the horse's natural home.|

runners_data.name: Barrys Spirit
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on good going and is lightly raced at five years old, making the form profile interesting. A natural hold-up runner pushed into midfield on the map by the weight of closers in this field — Flanagan's ability to find a clean run from a compromised starting point is the critical variable.|

runners_data.name: Heroes Rise
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes a rare ride back on this horse returning after 514 days absent; placed in five of last five completed runs over 2m-2m7f on good/soft, but the layoff length for a hold-up horse needing everything to fall right is a significant risk factor in a field this competitive.|

runners_data.name: Serienmond
runners_data.note: Apprentice Mr D McGill (7) up for the small McGill yard (T14 0/1); recent form shows little (7-5-10-9-6) and a sim-going record of 2W4P at OR 114 offers marginal claims — prominent style fits the shape but the form does not encourage confidence.|

runners_data.name: Elusive Ogie
runners_data.note: In reality a prominent racer who cannot secure that position in this congested pace scenario; form string includes an F and finishing positions of 8-5-10 over 2m-2m4f on good are not competitive at this level, and Daniel King will need fortune to be in front of traffic from a difficult tactical starting point.|

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer by nature but forced back by the density of pace in this field; McConnell's yard has shown T14 form (3/20), and Camlin Park won over 18f on good ground, but recent efforts of 7th-pulled-pulled suggest jumping reliability is a concern that Harvey must manage on a horse racing behind its natural position.|

races.paceDynamic: Red Glory is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one horse willing to lead, will dictate terms from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo over this 2m4½f trip on Good to Yielding ground. Chanceawetmorning, Liam Swagger, Theflyingbee, and Serienmond are all genuine prominent types who will push to race close to the pace, meaning the early positions just off the lead will be genuinely contested rather than handed freely. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — Elusive Ogie and Camlin Park are natural prominent racers who are unlikely to secure that position and will be shuffled back, while Barrys Spirit and Arctic Flame are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield due to the volume of closers in this field. With one uncontested leader setting a measured gallop, the race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or tracking just off the pace, as they will avoid trouble, travel in rhythm, and have first run at the final hurdles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Red Glory dictates an uncontested, honest but unhurried gallop and the prominent trackers conserve energy throughout.
scenarios.body: Red Glory sets the fractions from the front while Chanceawetmorning and Liam Swagger travel smoothly in his slipstream, with enough in reserve to mount sustained challenges jumping the final two hurdles. Good-to-yielding ground rewards horses with clean jumping and proven stamina, and this shape hands the race to those positioned to pounce without burning petrol early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Red Glory sets too strong a gallop early and burns himself out, leaving the prominent group emptying before the last.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a war of attrition from three out, and horses who have sat deepest with cover — Final Orders, Avalo, and Dreal Deal — arrive with a sustained run on the outside when the front rank fades. Good-to-yielding conditions with a stamina premium suit genuine stayers who travel economically and hit top gear late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Quickening Race
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely slow and the race turns into a sprint-finish from the home straight.
scenarios.body: Compact field positioning means horses with tactical speed and a sharp jump at the last hold the decisive advantage, rewarding those who have sat handy without over-committing; Chanceawetmorning and Theflyingbee both have the hurdles form and class to produce that burst. The slower early tempo partially neutralises the stamina edge of true stayers and brings the mid-division horses into play if they have tracked close enough.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely strong pace develops courtesy of multiple prominent types disputing fiercely early, setting it up for horses coming from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Arctic Flame and Heroes Rise, both true hold-up horses, would be the primary beneficiaries if the race is truly run at a searching tempo throughout; however, both are mapped out of their ideal position and Heroes Rise returns after a 514-day absence, making this a low-probability outcome. Barrys Spirit, a natural hold-up runner forced to race in midfield, would also need this exact shape to land a blow.

watchPoints.text: Heroes Rise has been off 514 days and Jack Kennedy's booking could mask a significant unknown — watch whether it shows any signs of greenness or ring-rustiness in the parade ring and early in the race.

Chanceawetmorning and Liam Swagger are both natural prominent types who will compete for the same berth just behind Red Glory — a contested early position between them could compromise both chances if neither settles cleanly.

Elusive Ogie and Camlin Park, both true prominent racers, cannot get their natural position and may push wider or get into trouble in a competitive early exchange — watch for either causing interference as they are squeezed back.

Final Orders returning after 137 days for Gavin Cromwell: the trainer's recent 7/28 strike rate suggests horses are coming back fit, but 137 days is a long time for a 10-year-old hold-up hurdler — monitor the pre-race odds movement for market confidence.

The going report consistently shows Good to Yielding across all races at Bellewstown today — any late watering or rail moves should be factored in, as Avalo has a pattern of disappointing on ground riding softer than standard good.

races.name: PANDA Mares Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Gordon Elliott ridden by Jack Kennedy, boasts a strong record on similar going (7 runs, 1W3P) and her recent form string including a third at Goodwood-style track conditions suits a strong late run over this trip; headgear worn (hood hurdle) noted, 28 days since last run is fine.

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who arrives on the back of a win 11 days ago for R Donohoe and Danny Mullins — excellent recent form (4 wins/5 places from 15 similar-going runs) makes this a serious contender if she can press from the front without over-committing early.

runners_data.name: Easter Bonnet
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins representative ridden by Brian Hayes, a genuine prominent type with distance form (won over 17f on Good) who pulled up last time, making her current fitness the key question; the step back up in distance from recent shorter efforts suits her historical profile.

runners_data.name: Fastnet Crystal
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up horse for Joseph O'Brien ridden by JJ Slevin, proven on soft ground with a win over 18f and placed at 16f on Good; not straightforward in consistency (fell/unseated form) but class and going-evidence make her a natural beneficiary of a well-run race from the front.

runners_data.name: Radar Ahead
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced mare whose genuine natural style is prominent racing, though the congestion of prominent types in this field means she is unlikely to secure that position — connections of T G McCourt have had a quiet 14-day strike rate and 45 days off adds a fitness query.

runners_data.name: Speisialta
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Anthony Black under apprentice Eoin Staples, won over 18f on Good and carries headgear (hood/tongue-tie) suggesting she needs rhythm from the front; 20 days since last run is ideal, and getting an uncontested lead is entirely plausible in this small field.

runners_data.name: Celtic Alliance
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced four-year-old for Gordon Elliott with only two career runs, both on Good or Soft, winning over 16f — the 125-day absence is a concern, and while he has the profile to run prominently, inexperience and the layoff make him the most uncertain runner in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Speisialta is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with a field of just seven, she should stride into an uncontested lead under Eoin Staples, setting a steady, controlled tempo on Good To Yielding ground over 2m1f. Daboya, Easter Bonnet, and Celtic Alliance are all prominent-style runners, but with Speisialta likely to dictate unchallenged, the prominent brigade will slot in behind rather than fight for the front — Radar Ahead is a genuine prominent type who has been redistributed to midfield in the map because those positions ahead of her are already contested. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural berth, and Speisialta and Daboya are best-placed to actually hold the lead and lead-chasing position respectively. A controlled, honest gallop on ground that has been riding consistently all afternoon favours hold-up horses with a strong late run, particularly those proven on Good-to-Yielding — Ardeen Joy and Fastnet Crystal, both patient-ridden, are the primary beneficiaries of a race shape where pace is metered rather than punishing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Speisialta Dictates, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Speisialta leads at a sustainable tempo and the prominent pack settle without pressure, triggering a stamina test in the final flight.
scenarios.body: Speisialta controls affairs from the front but sets no more than a fair pace, meaning the race unfolds as a test of class and finishing power from the second-last; hold-up operators who have been travelling smoothly throughout get the clearest sight of the win.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya and Easter Bonnet push forward early to pressure Speisialta, creating a proper pace and stringing the field out.
scenarios.body: A genuinely competitive gallop develops with Daboya and Easter Bonnet both committed to prominent positions, lifting the tempo enough to test stamina seriously; horses who handle the stronger pace from handy positions and jump well throughout benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Speisialta finds an unexpectedly clear passage at a generous clip and her pursuers leave it too late to close.
scenarios.body: Speisialta's recent winning form over course-appropriate going suggests she can be effective off the front if the rest of the field misjudges the pace, and a gallop that is honest but not outright strong can leave those held up too much to do; Eoin Staples controlling the fractions would be the key.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Outrun
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a genuinely fast tempo that leaves hold-up runners too far back to mount a challenge in the short Bellewstown straight.
scenarios.body: A pressured gallop forces Ardeen Joy and Fastnet Crystal to use energy earlier than ideal, and the race effectively becomes a stamina grind that rewards those who jumped fluently and travelled close to the pace throughout; this scenario is unlikely given Speisialta's natural tendency to control rather than force.

watchPoints.text: Speisialta must be watched at the start — if she misses the break or is forced to race off the pace for any reason, the entire race shape collapses and prominent types like Daboya become the controlling force.

Celtic Alliance is having his first run in 125 days for Gordon Elliott; a bounce-back or fitness deficit could see him drop away quickly from a prominent position, potentially affecting the jumpers behind him.

Radar Ahead is a natural prominent racer likely to find herself shuffled back further than ideal — watch whether Darragh O'Keeffe attempts to push her forward and what that does to the pace order in the early stages.

The Bellewstown straight is short, so horses making their move before the last flight rather than after it tend to be rewarded — watch which hold-up horses, particularly Ardeen Joy and Fastnet Crystal, are moving sweetest approaching two out.

Going is confirmed Good To Yielding for this race (despite the header listing Good To Soft), consistent with all other races on the card — runners with proven form on that precise surface have a genuine advantage and their going tags should be trusted.

races.name: John Purfield Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners_data.name: Codger's Rock
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer for Cian Collins, returning after 23 days in form that includes a placed effort over this distance on Good; sim-going record of six runs without a win needs to improve significantly, and from the back of an 18-runner field will need plenty of gaps to open.

runners_data.name: Garrick Painter
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-tie) applied, and the Simon Torrens booking for Noel C Kelly is notable after a 61-day break; tagged with a late-fade tendency and has won on similar ground, but from a true hold-up berth in a slowly-run race will find it hard to land a telling blow.

runners_data.name: Direct Approach
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, ridden by the in-form Jack Kennedy for Gordon Elliott; gets to dictate unchallenged here which is its best scenario, though it is technically racing outside its optimal role and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence — it has not won on soft-leaning ground over this trip.

runners_data.name: Tuckmill
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent runner for Peter Fahey, wearing headgear (tongue-tie) and now a ten-year-old with three wins at this sort of trip on Good — the amateur claim of McParland is a minor offset, but this is likely to be one of only two horses that actually secures an early prominent berth behind the leader.

runners_data.name: Convincing
runners_data.note: Lightly-weighted hold-up type who arrives in form after winning 18 days ago on Good; bumping up in class and distance from an eight-furlong Flat win is a query, but Eoghan Finegan's 5lb claim softens the weight, and the sim-going record is positive at this track.

runners_data.name: Masego
runners_data.note: John McConnell's four-year-old is unraced over this exact trip but has five runs showing consistent placed efforts including wins on Good; Alex Harvey rides and the horse carries the most promising recent profile of any non-front-runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Let It Settle
runners_data.note: Eight-furlong-winning-form runner whose 20-day turnaround for Thomas Hughes is neutral; zero wins in sim-going but finished second twice, and Phillip Enright will need a very kind run from the rear of this competitive 18-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Dictionary Corner
runners_data.note: J J Slevin booked and trainer has two winners from 12 in the 14-day window, which is the main positive; genuinely runs in last and has not placed in five starts on Good — displaced forward on the pace map, it is a true deep hold-up horse that needs pace to chase.

runners_data.name: Zarushio
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (tongue-tie) and has been off 105 days for Tom Dreaper — stamina at the limit is a concern, tagged with a fade tendency, and zero wins or places in six runs from the back of the field; a true hold-up runner in a race shape that will not produce enough early pace to assist.

runners_data.name: Chesterbaylad
runners_data.note: Won 23 days ago on Good for Ms Helen Markham, which is the headline form line here; Josh Williamson's 3lb claim helps offset top weight concerns, and while it is a genuine rear-runner shifted forward on the map, the winning momentum makes it the most interesting of the redistributed hold-up horses.

runners_data.name: Lunar Landscape
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe rides for Thomas Coyle, and the 16-day turnaround is sharp; five placed efforts but no wins, and the STYLE_FIT note reflects a horse that genuinely wants to come from last — in a small-field shape that is hard to exploit in an 18-runner race.

runners_data.name: Backinabit
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (blinkers) for Denis Hogan, who is active with two winners from 23 in 14 days; won over 17f on Good 20 days ago, so recent form and going are positive — however it is a true hold-up runner that will be nearer the back than the midfield position the map shows.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: Headgear (tongue-tie/cheekpieces), ran 11 days ago, and the fade tendency combined with a fall in recent form (F in latest) makes this difficult to recommend; Danny Mullins is a strong booking for David Budds but the horse has zero wins or places on similar going.

runners_data.name: Avandra
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and cheekpieces applied for P J Rothwell, who has three winners from ten in 14 days — that trainer angle is the live hook here; consistent in placed efforts on Good but never wins, and returning after 19 days will be doing its best work from a position further back than the map indicates.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Harry Sexton's 7lb claim for James Barcoe, back after just 10 days; won at 2m1f on Good two runs back, which is directly relevant, and sim-going record shows three places from 15 — a true deep hold-up runner that needs a stronger pace than Direct Approach is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Turlough Abu
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for V T O'Brien carrying a Reserve 1 booking which introduces jockey uncertainty; tagged with a fade tendency and has not finished better than fifth in eight career starts — a genuine hold-up runner with no win on Good going and limited upside here.

runners_data.name: Paymelater
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie, Reserve 2 booking, and trainer has zero recent winners from no runs in 14 days — compounding uncertainties; ran 17 days ago and has placed twice at this sort of trip, but is a genuine rear-runner whose pace map position is a consequence of redistribution, not its likely race position.

runners_data.name: Owl's Delight
runners_data.note: Reserve 3 booking introduces significant jockey uncertainty for R Donohoe; tagged with a fade tendency and has not placed in six runs on similar going — despite being one of only a handful of natural prominent types in the race, the booking concern and poor sim-going record are significant negatives.

races.paceDynamic: Direct Approach is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Jack Kennedy can dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo from the front on Good To Yielding ground — a surface that suits patient, relaxed jumping rather than an all-out gallop. With Tuckmill and Owl's Delight as the only other prominent types, the early fractions are unlikely to be truly searching, creating a race that plays out as a patient procession to the home turn before quickening in the final two flights. This shape heavily favours horses able to travel prominently or close to the pace in the first half, then pick up efficiently — pure hold-up horses relying on a wall of pace to close into will find their chance diminished. The field contains far more hold-up horses than the race shape accommodates naturally; Paymelater, Dictionary Corner, Zarushio, Chesterbaylad, Backinabit, Crypto Crash, Avandra, Surviving Murmansk, Lunar Landscape and Turlough Abu are all genuine rear-division types remapped forward, and in reality most will be at the back of a field where Direct Approach sets an uncontested, manageable pace — the horses most likely to actually secure a position close to the pace are Tuckmill and Owl's Delight, with Codger's Rock and Garrick Painter possibly grinding up from midfield. A controlled lead-and-wait shape suits prominent and close-mid runners who can track comfortably and deliver a clean run at the second-last.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Direct Approach Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Jack Kennedy is allowed to dictate a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the field settles in a long string behind him.
scenarios.body: Direct Approach leads at its own pace, the field strings out on the climb, and horses unable to get a clear passage from the rear are bottled up when the tempo quickens at the second-last; prominent trackers who have saved energy drafting the leader are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pick Off Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Direct Approach's lead is moderate but the horses close behind travel more easily and arrive full of running at the final flight.
scenarios.body: A small group of prominent and upper-midfield types tracks the leader without pressure, collects the advantage between the last two hurdles, and finishes strongly as the leader fades under weight; the Good To Yielding surface rewards those who have conserved energy in the first mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from halfway to create a true test and allow a resolute closer to make relentless late headway.
scenarios.body: A horse held off the pace in the first circuit finds the gaps opening as tired runners drift wide turning for home, clocking through to grab a place near the line; this scenario is materially discounted because most nominal midfielders here are redistributed hold-up types not naturally suited to the position they will occupy.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse And Hold-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so slow that it creates a bunched field and a sprint-finish over the final two hurdles, favouring an unexpectedly fresh closer.
scenarios.body: A compressed field means the rear-division horses are never far off the lead and a quick turn of foot in the straight settles it; this scenario is heavily discounted because the race structure points to a steady, manageable pace rather than a false gallop, and most genuine hold-up horses here are out of role.

watchPoints.text: Direct Approach (Jack Kennedy) is the only confirmed front-runner — watch how aggressively Kennedy elects to go and whether Tuckmill and Owl's Delight push for position early, as that will determine whether the pace is genuinely sustainable or a crawl.

Chesterbaylad arrives as the most recently-in-form hold-up runner and could be dangerous if Josh Williamson manages to find a prominent position early despite its natural inclination to race from the rear.

The Reserve jockey bookings on Turlough Abu, Paymelater and Owl's Delight mean three runners have late jockey changes confirmed — watch the declared riders at the final declaration stage, as an upgrade on any could shift their market position materially.

Masego (Alex Harvey) is unbeaten in three appearances when finishing in the first three on Good going and has quietly posted the most consistent placed profile in the race — monitor market moves before post time.

With 18 runners and a single pace-setter, the draw and starting position for hurdles races at Bellewstown will influence which hold-up horses can sneak closer to the pace than their natural style suggests — watch for early crowding at the first.

races.name: John Purfield Memorial Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Mc Swagger
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but has a noted tendency to fade in the finish; seven recent runs on similar going with no win and just one placing suggests limited upside, and a 41-day absence does not sharpen the outlook.

runners_data.name: Tropical Twist
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy in the saddle is a major positive; won over 17f on good ground and has a 1W1P record across 10 runs on similar going — strong stamina profile suits a steady-paced 2m1f race, and the 17-day turnaround is unconcerning for Gordon Elliott.

runners_data.name: Premier Rogue
runners_data.note: Noel Meade-trained stayer who has placed three times in nine runs on comparable ground; the 87-day layoff is a flag to watch, but three placing efforts at this sort of trip suggests he stays well enough to be involved if the race develops into a staying test.

runners_data.name: Kome Dans Un Reve
runners_data.note: Philip Fenton runner returning just 13 days after his last run; a genuine hold-up horse that will likely be further back than his midfield map position suggests — the fade-in-finish flag and a 0W0P record on similar going make it hard to make a case at the current odds, and racing out of his natural slot will not help.

runners_data.name: Laurie Blue
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old mare who carries the tongue-tie; a natural rear-division horse whose map position overstates her likely early position in a 17-runner field — her one win on similar ground came with a patient ride, and trainer E D Delany runs a small team with just one runner in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Syosset
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the race by form figures — four placings from five runs at 16-17f on good ground, and a genuine hold-up style that suits a compressed, late-developing race; John McConnell stable is in decent form at 3/20 in 14 days, and Eoin Staples takes the 5lb claim.

runners_data.name: Colin's Friend
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner returning after 204 days off; a true hold-up horse placed further forward on the map than he is likely to race, and the extended absence combined with a 0W0P record on similar going makes him hard to trust until he shows signs of a return to form.

runners_data.name: Kashel Spring
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who has run 0-0-0-0 in his last four starts, with his two career wins coming on much faster ground; his natural hold-up style will see him racing even further back than mapped in this large field, and recent hurdle form on soft or heavy ground has been deeply unimpressive.

runners_data.name: Grennanstown Lady
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane filly with a fade-in-finish flag and a 0W0P record in seven similar-going runs; operating from a true rear-division position despite the midfield map slot, and her form figures of 4/18f being her best recent effort suggest she needs further or a different surface.

runners_data.name: Frontier Rose
runners_data.note: Thomas Coyle runner with a string of mid-pack finishing positions on good ground and no win from 11 comparable-going runs; a natural hold-up horse whose races tend to follow the same pattern without a telling late challenge, and the 20-day turnaround is routine.

runners_data.name: Centaq
runners_data.note: The race's sole genuine front-runner, giving this analysis its backbone; ridden by 7lb claimer Alix Balfe, Centaq has placed three times in 15 similar-going runs but never won — the uncontested lead is his big advantage, though his OR of 80 sets a low ceiling and his jumping will need to be slick to hold on.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Liz Doyle runner who has placed four times in ten similar-going starts, suggesting he stays competitive without threatening to win; a true hold-up horse who will be deeper in the field than mapped, but his consistency at 16-17f on good ground makes him a minor-place player if traffic clears.

runners_data.name: Vairue
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran with just one win in 15 similar-going runs; mapped to midfield but a true hold-up type who will trail the main bunch, and at this age on a 10-day turnaround the concern is whether he retains enough class to get competitive at the business end.

runners_data.name: Lucky This Time
runners_data.note: Returning after 374 days off — by far the longest absence in the field — and has not placed in any of his five similar-going runs; tongue-tie and a pace-pair headgear note are details, but the fitness question after a year away is the dominant factor here.

runners_data.name: Doyen Og
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old running for the second time in 10 days with a fade-in-finish flag; his recent form of 7-8-7 on good ground at the same trip shows consistency without reward, and the quick turnaround for Adrian Sexton's small yard raises a mild stamina concern over 2m1f.

runners_data.name: Xquise
runners_data.note: No jockey listed in the declaration is a notable flag; recent form of 10th, 13th, 10th across a mixed range of trips suggests little confidence at any distance, and his best comparable-going run of 11/20f on soft barely qualifies him for this trip or this grade.

runners_data.name: Sonna Lady
runners_data.note: Four-year-old filly who has run 7th, 9th, 10th, and P in her last four starts, all over longer trips of 19-23f on good ground; no jockey named in the entry, and her form reverting to shorter suggests connections are exploring options rather than targeting a win here.

races.paceDynamic: Centaq is the lone confirmed front-runner in a 17-strong field and, ridden by apprentice Alix Balfe, will set a measured, uncontested gallop over this 2m1f trip on Good to Yielding ground — a sustainable pace that will not string the field out early. The bulk of the field is made up of genuine hold-up and midfield types, but the redistribution note is important: Laurie Blue, Kome Dans Un Reve, Kashel Spring, Colin's Friend, and Grennanstown Lady are all natural hold-up horses pushed onto the map in midfield because there are far more rear-division types than positions available — in reality, several of these will race further back than their map slot suggests, creating a compressed, slowly-developing race. With only one horse genuinely setting the fractions and a field largely inclined to race off the pace, the gallop is likely to be steady enough to compress the field, making the final two flights and the run-in decisive. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses with a sharp finishing kick who can travel efficiently in behind a single steady pace-setter and produce their effort late, with Syosset — who has shown consistent form figures placing in similar conditions — and Tropical Twist among the most natural beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Centaq Dictates, Late Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Centaq leads at a steady clip unchallenged and the field settles in a tight bunch behind, setting up a sprint finish from the last.
scenarios.body: Centaq's uncontested lead keeps the gallop honest but not brutal, ensuring the field travels as a group before the race ignites at the final hurdle; hold-up horses with tactical speed and clean jumping will surge past the tiring front-runner on the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Staying Types Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely slow and the race develops into a stamina test from 3 out, favouring those with proven staying ability.
scenarios.body: A dawdling tempo invites a bunched field where the race is won on class and grit from the home turn; horses with strong finishing histories in similar conditions and proven 2m+ stamina outlast rivals who struggle to maintain momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracking Wins
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Centaq in second or third from the outset, saves ground, and kicks decisively at the second-last before the true hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: Centaq's solo lead gifts a perfect stalking position to any runner willing to sit just off the pace, and the rider who secures that slot earns a clean run without traffic; this shape slightly disadvantages those stuck deep in the field in a compressed 17-runner race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the steady early pace is so uncontested that Centaq's rider dictates an economy-of-effort lead and the chasing pack never fully coordinates a challenge.
scenarios.body: Centaq's ability to control fractions entirely unchallenged allows it to conserve enough energy to hold on as the field disorganises behind; at OR 80 this is an upset scenario but the lack of any true pressing pace makes it a non-trivial possibility.

watchPoints.text: Syosset is the most consistent horse on form and the most naturally suited to a pace scenario where Centaq sets a steady gallop — watch whether Eoin Staples (5lb claim) gets a clean run through a 17-runner field in the straight.

Tropical Twist has Jack Kennedy booked and the most compelling trainer-jockey combination in the race — watch how Kennedy positions him from the gate, as an early move to track Centaq could be decisive.

Centaq's apprentice rider Alix Balfe (7lb) must dictate fractions cleanly; if Balfe is pressured into going too fast or misjudges the pace, the entire race shape collapses and the premium on front-running form evaporates.

Lucky This Time returns from 374 days off — watch his jumping early, as a horse this rusty in a 17-runner hurdle race represents a significant interference risk to horses attempting to travel on his inside or outside.

The going is Good to Yielding throughout the card despite the card listing Good to Soft — all five earlier races have been run on the same description, so expect no late surface deterioration to materially alter the pace map.
